stem: Sketch the graph of $y = {=a}\cos\theta {=signed(q)}$ for $\theta \in [0^\circ, 360^\circ]$ without using a table of values. What is the least value of $y$ on your sketch?
solution: The amplitude is $|a| = {=abs(a)}$: the graph of $y = \cos\theta$ is stretched vertically so that it rises ${=abs(a)}$ above, and falls ${=abs(a)}$ below, its midline.
The vertical shift $q = {=q}$ moves the whole graph, so its midline is the line $y = {=q}$.
The least value is the midline minus the amplitude: ${=q} - {=abs(a)} = {=q - abs(a)}$.

The sign of $a$ only decides where this lowest point is: at $\theta = 180^\circ$ when $a > 0$, and at $\theta = 0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ when $a < 0$ (the reflection in the $x$-axis). It does not change the value.
The least value of $y$ is ${=q - abs(a)}$.
notes: Standard: range reasoning from amplitude and shift. a runs over both signs so the student must use |a|, not a, for the distance from the midline: least value = q - |a| in every case (verified numerically over the whole parameter space against the sampled curve). |a| >= 2 so the coefficient always prints as a number; q != 0 so the shift always prints. Answer is a whole number, possibly negative.
